title: Edit AI Bezier Curve
content: ### Objective Edit AI Bezier curves with editing tools. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Edit Curvature 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. Click the point on the AI Bezier Curve to access the handle. 3. When the handle appears, click and drag the point on the desired end of the handle to change the curvature. ※Note: * To edit only one side's curvature, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard while click and dragging the point on the desired end of the handle. * To maintain the handle's angle while changing the curvature, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard then click and drag the curve. (ver MD10) #### Convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier Curve 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. To convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier curve, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard, and then click and drag the desired Segment Point. → The selected Segment Point is converted to an AI Bezier curve as the blue handle appears. #### Delete Handles 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar▶ Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2. Click the Segment Point on the curve. → The pair of handles appear. 3. Right click on the point on the desired handle to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Delete Point. Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. → The selected handle is deleted and the curve is converted to a straight line. ※Note: To delete the pair of handles at once, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and select the Segment Point on the curve.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for editing AI Bezier curves using various tools and techniques in a 2D pattern editing interface.

title: Mode
content: ### Objective Marvelous Designer provides total of five Mode as follows: Simulation, Animation, Modular, UV Editor and Sculpt Mode. ### Location Switch between Mode using the button on the right-top corner of the window. ### Operation Simulation Mode is a mode where it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D Window or animate draping of Garments, Poses, or Actions in the 3D Window. Animation Mode is a mode where it is possible to record, play and edit Garment animations. Modular Mode is a mode where it is possible to mix and match Garment components, such as sleeves and collars, as blocks to test and create new styles. UV Editor Mode is a mode where editing UV of Garment. (Ver. MD 7.5) Sculpt Mode Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. MD8)
content_description: Explore the versatile modes of Marvelous Designer, including Simulation, Animation, Modular, UV Editor, and Sculpt Mode, to create, animate, and customize garments with ease.

title: Internal Polygon/Line
content: ### Objective Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Polygon/Line ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar ▶ Internal Polygon/Line 2. Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. 4. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. 5. Use Length, Mirror Creation, and Position options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. Option | Description ---|--- Length | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) | Mirror Creating | The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Position | Left | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom | Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. 6. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. ※ Note: * Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. → An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. → An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). * Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. * Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines. ※ Note: Internal Shape Tool Group ※ Note: Mirror Creating
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for creating internal polygons and lines within a 2D pattern, utilizing various tools and options for precise design.

title: M:N Free Sewing (2D)
content: ### Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. * The difference in lengths between the first and second half seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it turns red to alert the user.
content_description: "Effortlessly create and manage sewing lines for multiple patterns at once using our M:N Free Sewing tool, enhancing your sewing efficiency and precision."

title: 3D File (Alembic) Import/Export
content: ### Objective Import/Export the object, cache, normal, and animation data contained within an Alembic file (ver2.4.0). ### Location #### Import Alembic Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Alembic #### Export Alembic Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (ver6.1) Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) ### Operation #### Import Alembic 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Alembic → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → The Import Alembic window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The Alembic file is imported based on the setting. Load Type | You can choose Open or Add. ---|--- Scale | Enter a number directly or select the desired values. Axis Conversion | Change the direction of each axis of the object. (ver. 2024.0) Option | Move Garment to Start Position | Navigates to the position of the start frame of the motion that imported the garment. Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Navigates to the position of the start frame of the motion that imported the outfit and avatar. Export Alembic 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic (HDF5) / Alembic (OGAWA) → The Open File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, click OK. → The Export Alembic window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click OK. → The file is exported as an Alembic file based on the setting. #### File | File Type (ver6.1) | Select a file type. ---|---|--- #### Object #### #### #### | Unweld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. #### Merge Vertex by Proximity: Merge vertices across patterns by proximity #### Unified UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. #### Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file. FPS | Sets the frame rate of the cache data. (below ver. 12.2) Basic | Scale the exported file by selecting the desired units or entering the percentage number. Animation | You can specify Entire Region or Play Region Only to export. Selecting the Current Frame menu allows you to export only the current frame. (ver. 2024.0) Color | You can export Strain or Stress as vertex color.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting Alembic files, detailing the necessary steps and options for managing object, cache, normal, and animation data.

title: Show Mesh
content: ### Objective Show or hide the mesh structure that 3D Garments are composed of. Mesh forms may vary depending on Patterns, Internal Lines, and Sewing state. ### Location #### 2D Pattern Window Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern Rendering Style ▶ Mesh #### 3D Garment Window Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment Rendering Style ▶ Mesh 3D Icon ▶ Garment Rendering Style ▶ Mesh
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to toggle the visibility of the mesh structure of 3D garments, allowing for a detailed examination of their composition based on various patterns, internal lines, and sewing states.

title: Create Additional Topstitch Style
content: ### Objective Create a new Topstitch style. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ +Add ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ +Add → A new item named Topstitch_1 is now being added with the same property of Default_Topstitch. ※ Note: * Additional items are added with names of Topstitch_1,2,3…. * If there are multiple Topstitch styles in the Topstitch tab when creating a Topstitch on a Pattern, click on the desired Topstitch style and create. * To create an additional Topstitch style with existing *.sst file, navigate to the Library ▶ Hardware and Trims ▶ Topstitch and drag and drop the desired Topstitch style to the Topstitch tab. Or, find the Topstitch file in the File Broswer window and drag and drop.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and adding new Topstitch styles within the Object Browser, ensuring ease of use and consistency in design.

title: Edit/Delete Tack
content: ### Objective Edit the position and the spacing of tacks/Avatar or delete unnecessary tacks. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack ### Operation #### Edit Tack 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack → The Garment is now being changed to semi-transparent. 2. Click ▶ drag on the end point to adjust the position and spacing. #### Delete Tack 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack 2. Click on a tack to delete. → The selected tack is now being highlighted in yellow color. 3. Press 'Delete' on the keyboard, or right-click and select Delete among the pop-up menu option. → The selected tack is now being deleted.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for editing the position and spacing of tacks or deleting unnecessary tacks in a sewing application.

title: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
content: ### ### Objective Edit Topstitch using the right-click pop-up menu. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch 2. Right click on the Topstitch to be edited. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Refer to below table and choose appropriate option in need. Option | Name ---|--- Select All With Same Property | All Topstitches that have the same properties with the selected one are selected. Assign to New Topstitch | A new Topstitch style is applied to the selected Topstitch. A new Topstitch style is created in the Object Browser when this option is selected. Delete | Delete the selected Topstitch. Add Internal Line on Topstitch (ver4.2.0) | Create an Internal Shape right on top of the selected Topstitch.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for editing Topstitch properties using the right-click pop-up menu in the 2D Toolbar.

title: Arrangement Property Setting
content: ### Objective Set arrangement property details after arranging patterns with Arrangement Points. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select 3D Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Arrangement ※ Note: The arrangement properties are only accessible for Patterns that are arranged by Arrangement Points. ### Operation 1. Arrange Patterns with Arrangement Points 2. Follow the guidelines below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select 3D Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Arrangement Point Name | Shows which arrangement point the selected pattern is on top of. ---|--- Shape Style | Changes the arrangement bounding volume pattern to be flat or curved. Position X | Moves horizontally according to the arrangement bounding volume. Position Y | Moves vertically according to the arrangement bounding volume. Offset | Adjusts the offset and curvature between the arrangement bounding volume and the pattern. Orientation | Changes the pattern's direction according to the arrangement bounding volume.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for setting arrangement properties of 3D patterns using Arrangement Points in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Deactivate (Pattern Only)/Activate
content: ### Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered nonexistent in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The general use of the function is to prevent complicated details, such as pleats or slits, from collapsing. When deactivating specific Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from the calculation. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Deactivate (Pattern Only) / Activate → The selected Pattern is now being deactivated/activated. ※ Note: 3D Statement
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on deactivating and activating Patterns in a 3D environment to enhance simulation speed and prevent detail collapse in garment design.

title: Corporate Firewall Setup and Allowlisting Marvelous Designer Endpoints
content: ### Applicable for: Enterprise users who are using corporate firewall and Allow-listing policies First, make sure you have corporate firewalls and allow-listing policies in place on your network systems. Please contact your company's IT or security team for this allow-listing and firewall setup. ### Note * Marvelous Designer authentication servers only allow HTTPS communication. Therefore, only port 443 is discussed in this article. * Until Marvelous Designer 10 version, the **verify: peer** option inside the Marvelous Designer 10 software was **disabled** , but from Marvelous Designer 11 version it is **enabled** and built and distributed. So if your company uses **SSL Inspection** on your secure network system, please check its detailed settings. * If you need to allow-list Marvelous Designer authentication servers for Marvelous Designer logins on a secure network, add the information below to your security solution. * If you are experiencing problems downloading in-app assets, please add the domain*.clo-set.com to your allow-list. * Non-firewalled customers may not need allow-listing of Marvelous Designer authentication servers. ### If you need allow-listing and use a corporate firewall * IPs to be allow-listed * 52.1.24.50 * 52.20.29.14 * Domains to be allow-listed * sapi.clo3d.com * sapi.clo3d-china.com * *.clo-set.com * Protocol and port to allow-listed * https (443 port) * Enable the Firewall option in Marvelous Designer login window (see the screenshot at the bottom) ### If you need allow-listing but don't use a corporate firewall * IPs to be allow-listed * 52.1.24.50 * 52.20.29.14 * Domains to be allow-listed * api.clo3d.com * api.clo3d-china.com * *.clo-set.com * Protocol and port to allow-listed * https (443 port) * Disable the Firewall option in Marvelous Designer login window (see below figure) ### Firewall option at Marvelous Designer login screen * Note that the information provided below is only for customers using enterprise firewall solutions, not Windows or macOS firewall features. Check with your company's IT or security team whether you use a firewall. ![Firewall=ON, Language=Global.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438418846873)
content_description: This web page provides essential guidelines for enterprise users on configuring corporate firewalls and allow-listing policies to ensure seamless access to Marvelous Designer authentication servers.

title: Fold Arrangement
content: ### Objective Fold Seam Allowances, collars and cuffs before activating the Simulation for better stability. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar ▶ Fold Arrangement ### Operation 1. After arranging Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar ▶ Fold Arrangement → The entire Internal Line/Shape of a 3D Garment appears. 2. Click on an Internal Line/Shape to fold. → The folding Gizmo appears. 3. Rotate the red or green axis along the blue circle as desired. → The selected area's Pattern is now being folded accordingly. → If the pattern is symmetrical, it is folded symmetrically. (ver 11) ※ Note: Folding Internal Line/Shape is also available after simulating/draping the Garment.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for folding seam allowances, collars, and cuffs in a 3D garment simulation to enhance stability during the design process.

title: Delete Pin
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary pins. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins → The selected pin is now being deleted. ※ Note: Selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on how to efficiently delete unnecessary pins from your 3D garment designs using various menu options and keyboard shortcuts.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Open/Save Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Save a created tape measure in .mea file format. Open a saved tape measure to reuse it. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Open /Save ### Operation #### Open Measurement 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Open → Open File window appears. 2. Select a desired file and click Open. #### Save Measurement 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Save → Save File window appears. 2. Select a desired location to store. 3. Enter a desired file name and click Save. → .mea file is now being created.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and opening tape measures in .mea file format within the Avatar Editor.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Delete Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Delete tape measures that are no longer in need. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Delete ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ Delete 2. Select a tape measure to delete. 3. Click on the Delete icon. → The selected tape measure is now being deleted.
content_description: Easily delete unnecessary tape measures from your avatar's measurements with a simple step-by-step process.

title: FILE: Export Joint Keyframe Animation with FBX
content: ### Objective Allows users to export both the garment and avatar together, without losing joint animation. The joint animation is currently exported with keys at every frame for the duration of the motion. ### Location File ▶ Export ▶ FBX ▶ Option ▶ Joint Animation ### Operation 1. Import an FBX containing a rigged character with joint animation as an Avatar, with the box next to 'Joint Animation' checked (found under the "Object" section). 2. Create a garment for the character, or add a garment option from the Library, at a desired pose from the Avatar's animation. → Simulate in the 3D Window to drape the garment onto the Avatar. 3. Once complete, navigate to the File menu location, select 'Export', then select 'FBX'. 4. Choose 'Export All' in the Export FBX pop-up window. 5. Click on 'OK'. 6. Open the resulting FBX file in another 3D software package. → Observe that the Avatar's joint animation has been exported (keyed at every frame).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to export a garment and rigged avatar together with preserved joint animation in FBX format.

title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
content: ### Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. ### Location #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard ※ Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu ▶ User Setting ▶ 3D ▶ Gizmo ▶ Divided Gizmo ### Operation #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Move by dragging in a desired direction. ※ Note: #### Move Y Axis Click > Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. #### Move X Axis Click > Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. #### Move Z Axis Click > Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. #### Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002535449) #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. → The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). 3. Click ▶ Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. ※ Note: #### Rotate Y Axis Click > Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. #### Rotate X Axis Click > Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. #### Rotate Z Axis Click > Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002843929)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Gizmo to move and rotate patterns, objects, and avatar joints in a 3D environment, detailing both default and user setup options.

title: Distribute
content: ### Objective Distribute Patterns or/and Internal Shapes/Lines by designated intervals (ver2.5.0). ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ Horizontally/Vertically ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Lines/Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ Horizontally/Vertically →The Distribute Window appears. 4. Enter the desired Spacing value and select OK. →The selected Patterns and/or Internal Lines/Shapes are distributed horizontally or vertically by the designated intervals.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for distributing patterns and internal shapes or lines at designated intervals using the right-click pop-up menu in the 2D toolbar.

title: Unified Gizmo
content: ### Objective Use an unified Gizmo to select, rotate and move elements. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click Pattern ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Click Pattern → Once a pattern is selected (clicked), the Unified Gizmo appears. ※ Note: Unified Gizmo can be set up at Preference. Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 3D ▶ Gizmo ▶ Unified Gizmo ※ Note: Gizmos for Avatars appear when X-ray Joint Points (Shift+X) is on or in OBJ format file.
content_description: This page provides guidance on using the Unified Gizmo within the 3D Toolbar to select, rotate, and move elements effectively.

title: Open/ Save Topstitch Style
content: ### Objective Open or save preset or custom Topstitch to easily use it in other Project or Garment files. ### Location #### Open Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Open #### Save Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Save ### Operation #### Open 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Open → The File Browser window appears. 2. Select the desired Topstitch file and click Open. → The selected Topstitch file opens and all properties are reflected in the Property Editor. #### Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Select Desired Topstitch Style ▶ Property Editor ▶ Save → The File Save window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and assign Topstitch name. Then, select Save. → The Topstitch is saved as a *.sst file and all properties are saved.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for opening and saving Topstitch styles to streamline their use in various projects or garment files.

title: Fasten/Unfasten Button
content: ### Objective Fasten or unfasten buttons to style the Garment as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button ### Operation #### Fasten Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button 2. Click on a button, then click on its corresponding buttonhole in either the 2D or 3D environment, then continue on to the remaining buttons and buttonholes. → The buttons move above the buttonholes. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes appear (ver2.5.0). #### Unfasten Button 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Fasten Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Fasten Button 2. Click on fastened buttons and buttonholes in either the 2D or 3D environment. → Buttons are now unfastened and return to their previous location. → Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes disappear (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: * To fasten multiple buttons and buttonholes at once, click and drag in the 2D window to select all buttons to be fastened, then click the first buttonhole to be paired with the buttons (ver4.0.0). * To unlock multiple buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on all fastened buttons and buttonholes. * Fastened buttons and buttonholes can now be moved (ver4.0.0).
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for fastening and unfastening buttons on garments using a 2D or 3D interface.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement
content: ### Objective Spread and arrange the entire or the selected patterns in the 3D window identical to 2D window state. ### Location #### Selected Pattern 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ right-click menu on a 3D pattern ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) #### All Pattern Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) ### Operation #### Selected Pattern 1. Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement identical to 2D window state. ※ Note: Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ right-click menu on a 3D pattern ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) → The selected Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state. #### All Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 2D Arrangement (All) → The entire Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for resetting the arrangement of 3D patterns to match their corresponding 2D layout, either for selected patterns or all patterns simultaneously.

title: Show Statistics (ver. 12.1)
content: ## Feature Overview You can check various information related to the garment through the 'Show Statistics' ## Steps Follow the indicated guideline below to open 'Show Statistics'. Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Statistics View Options icon (3D Window) ▶ Environment Display ▶ Show Statistics ## End Result Information related to the garment will be displayed at the left bottom corner of the 3D Window. ![hud_statistics.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438419772057) Please refer to the table below for the information items. Vertices | The number of the vertices ---|--- Edges | The number of the edges Triangles | The number of the triangular meshes Faces | The number of the entire faces Patterns | The number of the pattern pieces Trims | The number of the trims Sewings | The number of the Seam Line Pair Group CPUs | The number of the activated CPU Fps | Frames per Second, Simulation speed. F | Garment, gravity time I | Linear system time P | Garment-garment proximity time S | Garment-garment collision time O | Avatar skinning time SK | Avatar skinning + Joint animation time E | Time excluding clothing simulation and avatar skinning in the overall simulation. R | Rendering time. UI | UI update time. T | Simulation + Rendering + UI update time.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for accessing and interpreting garment-related statistics within the 3D Window of the application.

title: Reset Button Style Property
content: ### Objective Reset button item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset → The button item properties are now being reset back to default value.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for resetting button item properties to their default values in version 2.5.0.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide All Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Show or hide all of the tape measures in the window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements → All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to enable users to easily show or hide all tape measures associated with an avatar within the 3D display window.

title: Convert to Curve Point (AI Bezier Curve)
content: ### Objective Convert AI Bezier Curve's Segment Points to Free Curve Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point ### Operation #### AI Bezier Curve 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2. Right click on the AI Bezier Curve or the Segment point on the curve. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Convert to Curve Point. → The selected AI Bezier curve is converted to a Free Curve as its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and necessary Free Curve Points are added to maintain its original curvature. #### AI Bezier Curve Handles 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Curve Point 2. Click on the AI Bezier curve to be converted. → Its AI Bezier curve handles appear. 3. Right click on the end point of the handle and select Convert to Curve Point on the pop-up menu. → Its original curvature is maintained as Free Curve Points are added.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to convert AI Bezier Curve segment points into Free Curve points, ensuring the original curvature is preserved.

title: Apply Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Apply buttonhole styles or fabric material (.zfab) onto buttonholes as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ### Operation #### Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor 1. Click on a buttonhole and select a buttonhole style in the Property Editor. → The selected buttonhole style is now being applied to the buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to Selected Patterns → The buttonhole style is now being applied to the selected buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to New Fabric → A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for applying and managing buttonhole styles and fabric materials in the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: Create 2D Button Measurement
content: ### Objective View button position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. Select a button with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center 3. Select the desired 2D measurement options of the left/right/up/down. → The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for viewing and managing the 2D measurements of button positions within the Pattern outline using the Button Property Editor.

title: Button List Window
content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.
content_description: This web page explains the functionality and limitations of the Default Button style in the button creation process, highlighting its persistent nature and inability to be deleted after modification.
